memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "Go, sacrifice to your God here in the land." But Moses said, "That would not be right. The sacrifices we offer the Lord our God would be detestable to the Egyptians. And if we offer sacrifices that are detestable in their eyes, will they not stone us?"" - Exodus 8:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pharaoh has stopped saying no. Now he starts negotiating. Worship your God — but do it here, inside Egypt.

This is the oldest compromise there is. You can have your faith, as long as it stays within acceptable limits. Believe what you like, but do not let it change where you live or how you work.

Moses refuses immediately: that would not be right. He understood something crucial — worship on the enemy's terms is not worship. Israel could not be half-free and half-enslaved.

Many believers today live with this arrangement without noticing. Faith is kept in a box, allowed on Sunday, edited for the office, silenced in the family. It is Egypt's compromise: be religious, just do not actually leave.

Jesus called for something total: whoever wants to be my disciple must take up their cross and follow me (Lk 9:23). Not a corner of life, but all of it.

Where are you being invited to worship God without ever leaving Egypt?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which part of my life have I marked as off-limits to my faith?
2. Am I making compromises that keep me comfortable but not free?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I do not want a faith confined to safe places. Take every part of my life, whatever it costs. Amen.
